mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coincides with rising industrial production (INDPRO), creating a positive feedback loop that drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 20-day walk-forward, the correlation between HOUST and INDPRO lags behind S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05), or the 5-day return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: In at least 60% of such events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (p < 0.05), or the effect is indistinguishable from a flat yield curve (10Y-3M yield spread < 10 bps).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in union membership proxies (not available) suggests weakening labor market strength, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >15% in a month
failure_condition: Over 20 post-trigger observations, the 60-day return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or unemployment rate falls below 5% in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of industrial production (INDPRO) above trend while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3% indicates a supply-side expansion that supports S&P 500 20-day positive returns.
failure_condition: In 40% of similar supply expansions, the 20-day forward return is not positive (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% in at least two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% for three consecutive months triggers a negative feedback on equity valuations, producing S&P 500 5-day negative returns.
failure_condition: Over 20 such episodes, the 5-day return is not negative in more than 70% (p < 0.05), or UNRATE falls below 4% within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Co-movement between housing starts (not available) and retail sales (not available) would be ideal, but using HOUST and PAYEMS instead: when both show double-digit monthly gains, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive due to optimism in business and consumer activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% and PAYEMS increases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: In 50% of such events, the 20-day return is not positive (p > 0.05), or either proxy recovers less than 5% in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening of the 10-year yield relative to the 3-month yield (not directly observable) can be proxy-ized by FEDFUNDS approaching 5%. This signals a shift toward longer-term rate stability that supports S&P 500 60-day positive returns.
failure_condition: In 30% of such events, the 60-day return is not positive (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS reverts below 5% within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive quarters where industrial production (INDPRO) grows at a CAGR above 2% while unemployment (UNRATE) declines below 4% suggest robust supply-side expansion, predicting positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
regime_hint: supply chain and labor market improvement
failure_condition: Across 50 such supply expansions, the 20-day return is not positive in more than 40% (p > 0.05), or UNRATE rises above 4% in the next quarter.
